baptize verb

also baptise, christen, be baptized

late Latin

Vulg. Mt. 28.19
Vulg. Mc. 1.8
Tert. (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. baptize

baptīzō, baptīzāre, baptīzāvī, baptīzātum

verb, first conjugation

Greek βαπτίζω, “only in ecclesiastical Latin” (Lewis & Short). The rites word it differently: the Latin rite says Ego tē baptīzō in nōmine Patris, et Fīliī, et Spīritūs Sānctī; the Byzantine rite, with three immersions, says in the passive “the servant of God N. is baptized” (Βαπτίζεται ὁ δοῦλος τοῦ Θεοῦ).

Examples

  • euntēs ergō docēte omnēs gentēs: baptīzantēs eōs in nōmine Patris, et Fīliī, et Spīritūs Sānctī

    go, then, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy SpiritVulg. Mt. 28.19

  • Ego baptīzāvī vōs aquā, ille vērō baptīzābit vōs Spīritū Sānctō.

    I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.Vulg. Mc. 1.8

See also baptism, godfather, godmother, godchild.

SourcesLewis & Short: baptizo
